standard.title: Community spaces and outdoor settings
standard.description: participate in physical activities that utilise community spaces and outdoor settings, and evaluate strategies to support increased use of these spaces
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have participated in physical activities in natural and outdoor settings and analysed the steps and resources needed to promote participation (Y5-6). They can identify what supports participation but have not yet evaluated management strategies at a community level.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students participate in physical activities using community spaces and outdoor settings, and evaluate strategies to support increased use of these spaces.

nodes.label: Understanding community and outdoor spaces for physical activity
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify the range of community and outdoor settings used for physical activity in their local area and describe key features that make them suitable or unsuitable for different activity types.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two community or outdoor settings available locally for physical activity and describe one feature that supports or limits use of each.
nodes.typical_width: Map a range of local community and outdoor settings; describe what makes each suitable for different activity types; identify barriers to and enablers of participation in these settings.
wider: Investigate how urban planning and design decisions have shaped access to outdoor and community physical activity spaces in the local area, considering equity of access across different groups
Explore how different community groups use the same outdoor spaces and what this means for managing competing needs

response_modes.reason: Familiarity with a range of community settings is foundational for evaluating strategies — students who only know one space type have a limited basis for evaluation.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two community or outdoor settings available for physical activity
Describes at least one feature that supports or limits use of each setting

nodes.label: Participating in community and outdoor settings
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can participate in physical activities in at least one community or outdoor setting, demonstrating safe and appropriate use of the environment.
nodes.minimum_width: Participate in one physical activity in a community or outdoor setting, following safe and appropriate practices for that environment.
nodes.typical_width: Participate in activities across at least two different community or outdoor setting types; demonstrate awareness of environmental safety, minimal-impact practices, and appropriate behaviour for each setting.
wider: Participate in outdoor or nature-based activities such as bushwalking, orienteering or minimal-impact recreation, demonstrating understanding of environmental stewardship practices
Investigate First Nations Australian custodial approaches to Country/Place and apply principles from this understanding to participation in local outdoor settings

response_modes.reason: Participation with environmental awareness is a practiced disposition — students need repeated encounters in actual settings rather than simulated ones.

success_criteria: Participates in a physical activity in a community or outdoor setting
Demonstrates at least one practice appropriate to the safe and sustainable use of that setting

nodes.label: Evaluating strategies for increased use
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate strategies designed to support increased or sustainable use of community and outdoor physical activity spaces, weighing their benefits against potential drawbacks.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one strategy for increasing use of a community or outdoor space and give at least one reason why it would or would not be effective.
nodes.typical_width: Evaluate a range of strategies for managing, protecting and increasing use of community and outdoor spaces; consider environmental impact, community equity, and sustainability; design physical activity options that reimagine or better utilise community spaces.
wider: Investigate different approaches to custodial responsibility for Country/Place used by First Nations Australian communities, and evaluate how these principles could inform management of local physical activity spaces

Evaluate strategies used to manage and protect environments where physical activities take place (bushwalking trails, surf beaches, skate parks, sporting fields), identifying trade-offs between access and environmental protection

response_modes.reason: Evaluation requires students to apply criteria and weigh trade-offs — scaffold this with explicit criteria (e.g. effectiveness, equity, environmental impact, sustainability) before expecting independent evaluation.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Evaluation of community-level strategies connects to civic literacy, environmental stewardship and genuine community contexts — students who engage deeply here are building transferable critical evaluation skills with real-world application.
success_criteria: Identifies at least one strategy for supporting increased use of a community or outdoor physical activity space
Evaluates the strategy using at least one clear criterion (e.g. effectiveness, equity, environmental impact)
Weighs at least one benefit and one limitation of the strategy
